Radiology: Radiology encompasses diagnostic imaging modalities including chest X-ray interpretation for respiratory conditions and pneumoperitoneum detection, radiation safety practices such as patient exposure reduction and beam filtration, dental radiography involving material radiopacity and film processing, radiation biology mechanisms of tissue sensitivity and cell death, and technical domains like image quality optimization, grid application, and infection control in digital radiography systems.
Social & Preventive Medicine: Social & Preventive Medicine integrates epidemiological study designs (case-control, cohort), biostatistical analysis (confidence intervals, odds ratios, ROC curves), public health programs (NCD, RNTCP), vaccine efficacy, disease surveillance (AFP, HIV), and evaluation of preventive interventions, screening test validity, and population-level health policy through statistical modeling and program assessment.
Forensic Medicine: Forensic Medicine addresses brain death determination, forensic analysis of traumatic injuries (gunshot wounds, bite marks, inhalation burns, postmortem trauma), fetal age assessment, and child abuse identification. It integrates toxicological evaluations (poisoning, venom effects), medico-legal frameworks (autopsy protocols, criminal procedure codes), and injury pattern analysis (blast, chemical burns), alongside legal standards for abuse reporting and forensic documentation.
